title: All solid albums, but I would’ve liked to see nominations for Dead Ou...
transcript: I'm gonna rank the five musical theatre albums nominated at the Grammys. And quick explanation, I'm not really ranking them by how good the score is or by how well made the recording is, even if that is how the Grammy voters do it. I'm ranking it more by how well does it stand out as an ambassador for both the show and the music? For that reason, I think I'm gonna put Gypsy in last place. And it's not bad at all. It's totally solid. I like how complete it is. Obviously, the cast is great here. But there are just so many recordings of this musical already, I just don't think this recording is one that I'm gonna gravitate toward in the future. For a similar reason, in 4th place, I have Buena Vista Social Club. We don't get much of the story conveyed on this album, which, in a way, is fine, because I think the music is the strongest part of the this musical. So in that sense, they're putting their best foot forward. But in that case, I'd probably rather just listen to the original Buena Vista Social Club recordings. By contrast with Just in Time, even though I didn't really like this show, I think you do get the Jonathan Groff, Gracie Lawrence, Erika Henningsen stamp on this material. It's not necessarily a replacement for the original Bobby Darin recordings, but it just feels like its own animal. And I do think this album represents the show as a whole pretty well. In 2nd place I have Death Becomes Her, a pretty great representation of the show, actually. One of the things I really appreciated about the show, even though the music isn't really to my taste personally, is that the score is really well-integrated into the storytelling. It's well utilized to move us through the plot, take us on a journey and build up the comedic momentum, rather than disrupt it the way the music does in a lot of musical comedies. And that also comes through really well on the album. But in 1st place I have Maybe Happy Ending, which isn't only because it's my favorite musical on the list, I would also say it's the only one on the list where I actually liked the score more after listening to this album than I did coming out of the theatre. Walking out of the theatre, I loved the story, but felt like the music leaned a little bit on the basic side. But there is a sophistication and intricacy to it that comes out really beautifully on the album. But what about you? Feel free to tell me how you would rank these five albums, and if so, *how* are you ranking them? Because like I said, depending on how you're thinking about it, what you want out of a cast album, there is an argument to be made for putting these in basically any order.
classificationReason: Ranks 5 Grammy-nominated musical theatre cast albums covering multiple shows (Gypsy, Buena Vista Social Club, Just in Time, Dead Outlaw, etc.). Multiple shows discussed as a ranked list with no single primary focus.
